findings.statement: Across all seven complete tested carriers, unreduced q_o residual-incidence components have zero remote effects: a move in one component does not change any disjoint component's exact fixed-frame component state.

R/F/G safe forgetting splits residual-incidence connectivity in every tested geometry. In each case, some deleted residuals span two or more post-reduction components; a single deleted residual can connect as many as four post-RFG components on 4x4-k4.

After R is applied, moves can change disjoint components; RF, RFG and RFGH retain or increase such remote effects. The cross-component dependence is induced by global reduction semantics rather than present in raw q_o component dynamics.

Despite deleted bridge residuals and remote effects, monolithic R/F/G/H are reproduced with zero mismatches on all seven complete carriers by componentwise transforms plus a small global scheduler/boundary context.

A sufficient scheduler for the tested R/F/G/H factorization is: R -> global remaining P0/P1 move slots; F -> number of components with nonempty local blocked-frontier set capped at 2; G -> number of components with open columns capped at 2; H -> global open-column count capped at 2.

The frozen SAT2 component-multiplicity quotient is Q-V exact on all seven complete carriers. Its only observed nontrivial class reduction among those seven occurs on 5x3-k3, where full component multiset has 13,421 classes and SAT2 has 13,420.
That nontrivial 5x3-k3 SAT2 merge preserves scalar value but not transported action values or complete future behavior. Thus the tested corpus contains an exact Q-V merge that is not Q-A and not Q-F.

Component multiplicity parity (MOD2/XOR self-cancellation) fails Q-V and Q-A on every one of the seven complete tested carriers for the frozen post-RFG component definition. This rejects exponent-2 composition only at this component stage, not after a later quotient or valuation.

SAT3 is Q-F/Q-A/Q-V exact on the seven tested carriers but creates no observed class reduction relative to the full component multiset in those cases; it is therefore not yet evidence of a nontrivial count>=3 saturation law.

The reduction frontier has the shape of a scheduler-graded/contextual component monoid: component-local state is combined commutatively, while a small global scheduler acts on every component during normalization. Deleted residual bridges need not be restored wholesale to reproduce R/F/G/H.
